name: Wilbur Whateley
facts: His body underwent shrinkage and disintegration on the floor as witnessed by Dr. Armitage and Professor Rice.
Aside from face and hands, the really human elements in him must have been very small.
When the medical examiner arrived, there was only a sticky whitish mass on the painted boards.
He apparently had no skull or bony skeleton in any true or stable sense.
He had taken somewhat after his unknown father.
He left an almost interminable manuscript in strange characters, written in a huge ledger, adjudged a diary.
He and Old Whateley always paid their debts with ancient gold, no trace of which has been found.
Sally Sawyer says he 'come to the bad eend he desarved' and was not all human himself.
Sally believes he and Old Whateley raised something in the nailed-up house that is even less human than he was.
fate: Died and his body disintegrated into a sticky whitish mass, according to Sally Sawyer he 'come to the bad eend he desarved.'

sources.quote: When the medical examiner came, there was only a sticky whitish mass on the painted boards, and the monstrous odor had nearly disappeared. Apparently Whateley had had no skull or bony skeleton; at least, in any true or stable sense. He had taken somewhat after his unknown father.
No trace of the ancient gold with which Wilbur and Old Whateley always paid their debts has yet been discovered.

I tell ye, Mis' Corey, they's suthin' abroad as hadn't orter be abroad, an' I fer one think that black Wilbur Whateley, as come to the bad eend he desarved, is at the bottom of the breedin' of it. He wa'n't all human hisself, I allus says to everybody

name: Dr. Armitage
facts: He witnessed the frightful changes taking place on the floor along with Professor Rice.

sources.quote: One need not describe the kind and rate of shrinkage and disintegration that occurred before the eyes of Dr. Armitage and Professor Rice

name: Professor Rice
facts: He witnessed the frightful changes taking place on the floor along with Dr. Armitage.

sources.quote: One need not describe the kind and rate of shrinkage and disintegration that occurred before the eyes of Dr. Armitage and Professor Rice

name: Earl Sawyer
facts: He tended the horse and cattle during Wilbur's absence.
He developed a woefully acute case of nerves.

sources.quote: Earl Sawyer, who tended the horse and cattle during Wilbur's absence, had developed a wofully acute case of nerves.

name: Luther Brown
facts: He was the hired boy at George Corey's.
He rushed frenziedly back from his morning trip to Ten-Acre Meadow with the cows on the morning of September tenth.
He was almost convulsed with fright as he stumbled into the kitchen.
He tried to stammer out his tale to Mrs. Corey about strange tracks and smells near the glen.
He faltered and seemed to shiver afresh with the fright that had sent him flying home.

sources.quote: About 7 o'clock Luther Brown, the hired boy at George Corey's, between Cold Spring Glen and the village, rushed frenziedly back from his morning trip to Ten-Acre Meadow with the cows.
Here he faltered, and seemed to shiver afresh with the fright that had sent him flying home.

name: Mrs. Corey
facts: Luther Brown stammered out his tale to her.
She began telephoning the neighbors after being unable to extract more information from Luther, starting the overture of panic.
She called Sally Sawyer, housekeeper at Seth Bishop's.

sources.quote: Mrs. Corey, unable to extract more information, began telephoning the neighbors; thus starting on its rounds the overture of panic that heralded the major terrors.

name: George Corey
facts: Luther Brown was the hired boy at his farm, located between Cold Spring Glen and the village.

sources.quote: About 7 o'clock Luther Brown, the hired boy at George Corey's, between Cold Spring Glen and the village, rushed frenziedly back from his morning trip to Ten-Acre Meadow with the cows.

name: Sally Sawyer
facts: She was housekeeper at Seth Bishop's, the nearest place to Whateley's.
Her boy Chauncey, who slept poorly, had gone up on the hill toward Whateley's and dashed back in terror.
She relayed Chauncey's account to Mrs. Corey over the party telephone line.
She believes black Wilbur Whateley was at the bottom of the breeding of the horror.
She says there have always been unseen, non-human things around Dunwich that are not good for human folks.
She feels that something awful is about and that her time is nigh.

She warns that Cold Spring Glen is not a healthy or decent place, where whippoorwills and fireflies do not act like creatures of God, and strange things can be heard rushing and talking in the air between the rock falls and Bear's Den.

sources.quote: When she got Sally Sawyer, housekeeper at Seth Bishop's, the nearest place to Whateley's, it became her turn to listen instead of transmit
They's allus ben unseen things araound Dunwich—livin' things—as ain't human an' ain't good fer human folks.
I know suthin' awful's abaout, an' feel my time is nigh, though only Gawd knows jest what it is.

I allus says Col' Spring Glen ain't no healthy nor decent place. The whippoorwills an' fireflies there never did act like they was creaters o' Gawd, an' they's them as says ye kin hear strange things a-rushin' an' a-talkin' in the air daown thar ef ye stand in the right place, atween the rock falls an' Bear's Den.

name: Chauncey
facts: He is Sally Sawyer's son, who sleeps poorly.
He had gone up on the hill toward Whateley's and dashed back in terror after one look at the place and the pasturage.
He came back running and could hardly talk for being scared.
He reported that Old Whateley's house was all blown up, with timbers scattered as if by dynamite, and the bottom floor covered in a tarlike substance.
He reported awful round marks in the yard, bigger than a hogshead, sticky like the stuff on the house, leading into the meadows in a wide matted swath with stone walls tumbled.
He went to look for Seth's cows and found them in the upper pasture near the Devil's Hop Yard in an awful shape, half gone and half sucked dry of blood with sores.
He thought the swath led toward the glen road to the village.
He heard whippoorwills so loud in Cold Spring Glen that he couldn't sleep, and a faint ripping or tearing sound of wood like a big box being opened.
He got no sleep until sunup, then went to Whateley's to see what was the matter.

sources.quote: for Sally's boy Chauncey, who slept poorly, had been up on the hill toward Whateley's, and had dashed back in terror after one look at the place, and at the pasturage where Mr. Bishop's cows had been left out all night.

He says Ol' Whateley's haouse is all blowed up, with the timbers scattered raound like they'd ben dynamite inside; only the bottom floor ain't through, but is all covered with a kind o' tarlike stuff that smells awful an' drips daown offen the aidges onto the graoun' whar the side timbers is blowed away.

towards mornin' Cha'ncey he heerd the whippoorwills so laoud in Col' Spring Glen he couldn't sleep none. Then he thought he heerd another faintlike saound over towards Wizard Whateley's—a kinder rippin' or tearin' o' wood, like some big box or crate was bein' opened fur off.

name: Seth Bishop
facts: Sally Sawyer was housekeeper at his place, the nearest to Whateley's.
His cows were left out all night in the pasturage and were found in an awful shape, half gone and half sucked dry of blood.
He went out to look at the cattle himself, though Sally doubts he wants to get very near Wizard Whateley's.

sources.quote: Seth he's gone aout naow to look at 'em, though I'll vaow he wun't keer ter git very nigh Wizard Whateley's!

name: Old Whateley
facts: He and Wilbur always paid their debts with ancient gold, no trace of which has been found.
Sally Sawyer believes he and Wilbur raised something in the nailed-up house that is even less human than Wilbur was.
His house is described as being near Cold Spring Glen and has an awful stench.

sources.quote: an' I think he an' Ol' Whateley must a raised suthin' in that there nailed-up haouse as ain't even so human as he was.

name: Dunwich
facts: Men were sent there to look up property and notify heirs of the late Wilbur Whateley.
The countryside was in great agitation because of growing rumblings beneath the domed hills and unwonted stench and sounds from Whateley's farmhouse.
Sally Sawyer says there have always been unseen, non-human things around Dunwich.

sources.quote: They found the countryside in great agitation, both because of the growing rumblings beneath the domed hills, and because of the unwonted stench and the surging, lapping sounds which came increasingly from the great empty shell formed by Whateley's boarded-up farmhouse.
They's allus ben unseen things araound Dunwich—livin' things—as ain't human an' ain't good fer human folks.

name: Aylesbury
facts: Men were sent to Aylesbury as well as Dunwich to look up property and notify heirs.
A ponderous report was filed at the court-house in Aylesbury regarding heirship of the deceased's estate.

sources.quote: They filed a ponderous report at the court-house in Aylesbury, and litigations concerning heirship are said to be still in progress amongst the innumerable Whateleys, decayed and undecayed, of the upper Miskatonic valley.

name: Miskatonic University
facts: Wilbur Whateley's manuscript and collection of strange books were sent there for study and possible translation.

sources.quote: After a week of debate it was sent to Miskatonic University, together with the deceased's collection of strange books, for study and possible translation

name: upper Miskatonic valley
facts: Litigations concerning heirship of the Whateley estate are said to be still in progress among the innumerable Whateleys of the upper Miskatonic valley.

sources.quote: litigations concerning heirship are said to be still in progress amongst the innumerable Whateleys, decayed and undecayed, of the upper Miskatonic valley.

name: Cold Spring Glen
facts: Luther Brown's route with the cows was between Cold Spring Glen and the village.
Strange tracks and smells were found in the road beyond the glen.
Chauncey heard whippoorwills so loud in Cold Spring Glen he couldn't sleep.

Sally Sawyer says Cold Spring Glen is not a healthy or decent place, where whippoorwills and fireflies don't act like creatures of God and strange things can be heard rushing and talking in the air between the rock falls and Bear's Den.

sources.quote: About 7 o'clock Luther Brown, the hired boy at George Corey's, between Cold Spring Glen and the village, rushed frenziedly back from his morning trip to Ten-Acre Meadow with the cows.

I allus says Col' Spring Glen ain't no healthy nor decent place. The whippoorwills an' fireflies there never did act like they was creaters o' Gawd, an' they's them as says ye kin hear strange things a-rushin' an' a-talkin' in the air daown thar ef ye stand in the right place, atween the rock falls an' Bear's Den.

name: Ten-Acre Meadow
facts: Luther Brown made his morning trip there with the cows when he encountered the horror.

sources.quote: rushed frenziedly back from his morning trip to Ten-Acre Meadow with the cows.

name: Wizard Whateley's ol' haouse
facts: The house was boarded up and emitted a surging, lapping sound and unwonted stench.
The house was reported to be all blown up, with timbers scattered as if by dynamite.
The bottom floor was still intact and covered with a tarlike substance that smelled awful and dripped from the edges.
A faintlike ripping or tearing sound of wood was heard near the house, like a big box being opened.

sources.quote: the surging, lapping sounds which came increasingly from the great empty shell formed by Whateley's boarded-up farmhouse

He says Ol' Whateley's haouse is all blowed up, with the timbers scattered raound like they'd ben dynamite inside; only the bottom floor ain't through, but is all covered with a kind o' tarlike stuff that smells awful an' drips daown offen the aidges onto the graoun' whar the side timbers is blowed away.

name: Devil's Hop Yard
facts: Seth Bishop's cows were found in the upper pasture nigh the Devil's Hop Yard, in an awful shape.

sources.quote: an' faound 'em in the upper pasture nigh the Devil's Hop Yard in an awful shape.

name: Bear's Den
facts: Sally Sawyer says strange things can be heard rushing and talking in the air in Cold Spring Glen between the rock falls and Bear's Den.

sources.quote: ye kin hear strange things a-rushin' an' a-talkin' in the air daown thar ef ye stand in the right place, atween the rock falls an' Bear's Den.
